title: Correspondence Approach to Time-Dependent Decaying Quantized Fields
content: We present a correspondence-principle framework that maps a classical field-amplitude decay law \( \Gamma(t) \) onto the quantum master equation for the associated quantized mode. After reviewing representative classical regimes; exponential (Ohmic relaxation); diffusive (\( t^{-1/2} \)); power-law (\( t^{-1} \)); oscillatory damped; stretched-exponential (Kohlrausch--Williams--Watts); and multi-mode quasi-normal-mode expansions; we derive a generalized master equation for a single bosonic mode whose complex amplitude is \( \alpha\,\Gamma(t) \), with \( \alpha \) in general complex and \( \Gamma(t) \) an arbitrary real, positive, differentiable envelope. The resulting dynamics is \( \dot{\rho}=\gamma(t)\bigl(a\rho a^{\dagger}-\tfrac12\{a^{\dagger}a,\rho\}\bigr) \) with time-dependent rate \( \gamma(t)\coloneqq-2\dot{\Gamma}(t)/\Gamma(t) \); it reduces to the standard amplitude-damping Lindblad equation for \( \Gamma(t)=\exp(-\gamma t/2) \) and preserves the coherent-state form \( |\alpha\,\Gamma(t)\rangle\langle\alpha\,\Gamma(t)| \). This provides a unified quantum-optical description of dissipation in conductive media; disordered dielectrics; and open resonators.
